newsitem.title: USA: PepsiCo debt inactive despite news of charge.
newsitem.headline: PepsiCo debt inactive despite news of charge.

text.p: Cola wars have yet to cause any casualties in the fixed-income markets as major bottlers find themselves faced with new challenges, analysts said.

Despite trouble brewing for PepsiCo Inc in its Latin American bottling operations and the company's forecast for dwindling third quarter earnings, the company's debt has been inactive, traders and analysts said.
On Thursday, PepsiCo said it planned to restructure its international operations and take a $525 million charge.
Based on past performance, however, analysts said the company should be able to ward off this and further tribulations.

"For a high-quality credit like PepsiCo this type of maneuver really doesn't have any substantive effect whatsoever," said a corporate strategist at a big New York shop, adding that he does not expect any market reaction.
"You'd need a nuclear missile strike to hurt it," he said.
Mark Altherr, an industrial debt analyst at Salomon Brothers, concurred and said there would need to be a string of negative news to tarnish the beverage giant's credit.

"If this were to continue and earnings were permanently weaker, you might see some pressure on the ratings." he said. "It's a strong credit and they really haven't done anything bad to the balance sheet."
A Standard & Poor's bottling analyst would only say the agency was reviewing PepsiCo in light of restructuring news.

Pepsi debt was inactive with no quoted markets. Altherr said the debt would "probably trade a little less well" should it become active. A move of even five basis points is considered rash for the credit, he noted.

Rival Coca-Cola Co debt was also inactive. Coca-Cola Enterprises $300 million 30-year notes, priced to yield 33 basis points over U.S. Treasuries on Wednesday, were lifted by overall market technicals and traded around 31 or 32 basis point on Friday, dealers said.
Traders at several big New York shops said both Coca-Cola and PepsiCo debt rarely trades.
What might normally signal a boon to Coca-Cola and Coca-Cola Enterprises has been largely offset by Coke's acquisitional strategies, Altherr said.

"They are increasing the Coca-Cola Cos debt leverage by having their affiliate Coca-Cola Enterprises buy various bottling operations overseas, Altherr said. Coca-Cola Enterprises debt widened modestly in June after the company said it would buy the U.K. bottler of Coca-Cola and Cadbury Schweppes Plc for $1.85 billion.
"That's more of a concern than the positives here," he said, adding that because it's Coca-Cola one would assume the company will perform well.
Equity markets have shown more interest in PepsiCo's negative news. PepsiCo shares were down 1-3/4 point at 28-1/2 at 1500 EDT/1900 GMT. Coca-Cola was off 1/2 point at 51.
